## typography_lettering_art

> Hand-lettered art piece — a single phrase rendered as the visual subject.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1024x1024`, aspect `1:1`
**Demo vars:** `templates/typography/_vars_examples/typography_lettering_art.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A square hand-lettered art piece whose subject is the phrase "Slow craft, steady hand.". The phrase is rendered as drawn lettering — every stroke is custom-built rather than typeset — and occupies the bulk of the frame as the visual artwork. A small attribution line "Lettering by House of Iris" sits as a quiet footer. No scenery, no illustration, no figures — only ink on paper.
[2. Action] The composition rewards close reading: the eye traces the primary letterform contours, follows their custom ligatures and flourishes, then settles on the small footer credit. The piece must read as a single considered drawing rather than a slogan poster — the lettering IS the artwork.
[3. Scene] A textured paper surface — warm cream cotton-rag stock with faint deckle — fills the frame. No staging, no environment; the paper is the world. Subtle paper grain is preserved but never overwhelming, so the lettering stays the dominant subject.
[4. Composition] Square 1:1 frame. The phrase occupies roughly the central 78% of the canvas, balanced as a single shape with internal rhythm rather than rigid line stacking. Generous breathing space at the corners. The sub-credit sits as a thin centered line in the bottom 8% safe band. Lettering style: high-contrast didone-flavored brush script.
[5. Style] Studio lettering aesthetic in the lineage of Jessica Hische, House Industries, Tobias Frere-Jones lecture posters. Ink color: deep walnut ink, almost black, sitting on the warm paper. Strokes show drawn weight contrast — thicks and thins, custom terminals, considered counters. No fonts pressed flat — every glyph is composed for this phrase. Matte, ink-on-paper finish with no glow, no 3D, no digital chrome.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- phrase_main: "Slow craft, steady hand."
- sub_credit: "Lettering by House of Iris"

NO: typeset fonts pressed flat, photographic imagery, human figures, 3D extrusion, rainbow gradients, watermarks, drop shadows, lens flare, clip-art ornaments, real famous foundry names, neon glow, stock-photo backgrounds
```

## typography_specimen_poster

> Type specimen poster — display alphabet, glyph grid, and typeface metadata as the artwork.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1024x1280`, aspect `4:5`
**Demo vars:** `templates/typography/_vars_examples/typography_specimen_poster.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A type specimen poster for the typeface "Murmur Grotesk", drawn by Iris Calder at the Medium 500 weight. The poster is a single composed plate where the type itself is the subject — letterforms are rendered at display size and treated as drawn artwork rather than running copy. No human figures, no products, no scenery — only typography and the paper it sits on.
[2. Action] The viewer's eye lands first on the oversized headline glyph cluster, drops to a generously letterspaced alphabet line, and then scans a small glyph grid showing case, numerals, and diacritics. Below that, a single sample pangram demonstrates the typeface in body-size context. The reading rhythm is slow and deliberate, like turning a foundry catalog page.
[3. Scene] Studio-flat document setting. The poster sits against a calm paper-white field with a faint warm-grey paper grain, calibrated for both screen and offset reproduction. No environment, no perspective, no objects — the page is the world.
[4. Composition] Vertical 4:5 plate. Top ~38% holds an oversized display letter-cluster bleeding to a comfortable margin. A horizontal rule separates it from a banner alphabet line spanning the full width. Below the alphabet, a 4-row x 9-column glyph grid occupies the central band. A footer block holds the typeface name, designer credit, weight, classification, and the sample pangram, set quietly. 5% safe margins on every edge.
[5. Style] Foundry-catalog editorial aesthetic — Klim, Commercial Type, Schick Toikka style. Palette is restrained: deep ink-black on paper-white with a single muted accent (oxidized teal or warm ochre) on the rule and the small caps labels. No gradients, no glow, no drop shadows; only the typeface itself, set with confident hierarchy. Print-ready, vector-clean.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- typeface_name: "Murmur Grotesk"
- designer_credit: "Drawn by Iris Calder"
- weight_label: "Medium 500 / Neo-Grotesque Sans"
- sample_pangram: "Sphinx of black quartz, judge my vow."

NO: decorative illustration, photographic imagery, human figures, product mockups, real famous foundry logos, copyrighted commercial typeface names, rainbow palette, drop shadows, 3D extrusion, watermarks, clip-art ornaments, lens flare
```
